title: Product search and catalogue on the shop and the public product API

sourcesRead.contributes: user story, context (UI page, API endpoints, out of scope), Gherkin AC-1..AC-11, PO clarification replacing AC-4

actors: a shopper on Automation Exercise; a partner app using the public product API (story.md#L17)
context: Products page /products shows the whole catalogue under "All Products" with a "Search Product" search box and a search button; API on the same host with form-encoded requests: GET /api/productsList (whole catalogue) and POST /api/searchProduct with parameter search_product (story.md#L23-L26). Search terms are plain words or phrases, e.g. jean, top, dress, Men Tshirt (story.md#L27).
outOfScope: punctuation and special characters in search terms (tracked separately) (story.md#L28)
browsing by brand, which is AE-3 (story.md#L103)

acceptanceCriteria.quote:
Scenario: AC-1 Catalogue is available through the API
    When a client calls GET /api/productsList
    Then the response lists the products of the catalogue in a "products" array
    And every product has an "id", a "name", a "price", a "brand" and a "category"
    And the category holds the audience ("usertype", e.g. Women, Men, Kids) and the category name
    And every price is written as "Rs. " followed by the amount, e.g. "Rs. 500"
acceptanceCriteria.text: Catalogue is available through the API: GET /api/productsList lists the products of the catalogue in a "products" array; every product has an "id", a "name", a "price", a "brand" and a "category"; the category holds the audience ("usertype", e.g. Women, Men, Kids) and the category name; every price is written as "Rs. " followed by the amount, e.g. "Rs. 500".
outcomes: the response lists the catalogue products in a "products" array
every product has an "id", a "name", a "price", a "brand" and a "category"
every category holds the audience "usertype" (e.g. Women, Men, Kids) and the category name
every price is "Rs. " followed by the amount, e.g. "Rs. 500"

acceptanceCriteria.quote:
Scenario: AC-2 Search by a term through the API
    When a client posts search_product = "jean" to /api/searchProduct
    Then exactly these products are returned: "Soft Stretch Jeans", "Regular Fit Straight Jeans", "Grunt Blue Slim Fit Jeans"
acceptanceCriteria.text: Search by a term through the API: posting search_product = "jean" to /api/searchProduct returns exactly these products: "Soft Stretch Jeans", "Regular Fit Straight Jeans", "Grunt Blue Slim Fit Jeans".
outcomes: search_product = "jean" returns exactly "Soft Stretch Jeans", "Regular Fit Straight Jeans", "Grunt Blue Slim Fit Jeans"
no other product is returned

acceptanceCriteria.quote:
Scenario: AC-3 Search ignores letter case
    When a client searches for "TOP" and for "top"
    Then both searches return the same products
acceptanceCriteria.text: Search ignores letter case: searching for "TOP" and for "top" returns the same products.
outcomes: searching "TOP" and searching "top" return the same products

acceptanceCriteria.quote:
Scenario: AC-4 Search matches product names
    When a client searches for "dress"
    Then every product returned has the term in its product name
    And every catalogue product whose name contains "dress" is returned
acceptanceCriteria.text: Search matches the product name or its category name (AC-4 as replaced by the Product Owner clarification of 2026-09-26): searching "dress" returns every product whose name contains "dress" plus every product in a "Dress" category, even if the word is not in its name, and nothing else; the brand is not a search field.
outcomes: searching "dress" returns every catalogue product whose name contains "dress" (case-insensitive)
searching "dress" also returns every product in a "Dress" category, even if the word is not in its name, e.g. "Sleeves Top and Short - Blue & Pink" (Kids > Dress)
nothing else comes back: every product returned has "dress" in its name or its category name
searching "Polo" only finds products with "Polo" in the name or category (the brand is not a search field)

acceptanceCriteria.quote:
Scenario: AC-5 Nothing matches
    When a client searches for "zzqxv"
    Then an empty product list is returned, not an error
acceptanceCriteria.text: Nothing matches: searching for "zzqxv" returns an empty product list, not an error.
outcomes: searching "zzqxv" returns an empty product list
the response is not an error

acceptanceCriteria.quote:
Scenario: AC-6 Search without a term (empty value)
    When a client posts search_product with an empty value
    Then the whole catalogue is returned, the same products as GET /api/productsList
acceptanceCriteria.text: Search without a term (empty value): posting search_product with an empty value returns the whole catalogue, the same products as GET /api/productsList.
outcomes: search_product with an empty value returns the whole catalogue
the products are the same as GET /api/productsList returns

acceptanceCriteria.quote:
Scenario: AC-7 Search without a term (parameter missing)
    When a client posts to /api/searchProduct without the search_product parameter
    Then the request is rejected with response code 400
    And the message is "Bad request, search_product parameter is missing in POST request."
acceptanceCriteria.text: Search without a term (parameter missing): posting to /api/searchProduct without the search_product parameter is rejected with response code 400 and the message "Bad request, search_product parameter is missing in POST request."
outcomes: response code 400
message "Bad request, search_product parameter is missing in POST request."

acceptanceCriteria.quote:
Scenario: AC-8 Search from the Products page
    Given a shopper on the Products page
    When they type "jean" in the search box and press the search button
    Then the product grid is headed "Searched Products"
    And the search box still shows "jean"
    And exactly the three jeans products listed in AC-2 are shown
acceptanceCriteria.text: Search from the Products page: a shopper on the Products page types "jean" in the search box and presses the search button; the product grid is headed "Searched Products", the search box still shows "jean", and exactly the three jeans products listed in AC-2 are shown.
outcomes: the product grid is headed "Searched Products"
the search box still shows "jean"
exactly "Soft Stretch Jeans", "Regular Fit Straight Jeans", "Grunt Blue Slim Fit Jeans" are shown

acceptanceCriteria.quote:
Scenario: AC-9 Searching from the Products page without a term
    Given a shopper on the Products page
    When they leave the search box empty and press the search button
    Then the grid is headed "All Products"
    And every product of the catalogue (GET /api/productsList) is shown
acceptanceCriteria.text: Searching from the Products page without a term: a shopper on the Products page leaves the search box empty and presses the search button; the grid is headed "All Products" and every product of the catalogue (GET /api/productsList) is shown.
outcomes: the grid is headed "All Products"
every product GET /api/productsList returns is shown

acceptanceCriteria.quote:
Scenario Outline: AC-10 The shop and the API agree on search results
    When a shopper searches for "<term>" on the Products page
    Then the products shown are exactly the products POST /api/searchProduct returns for "<term>"

    Examples:
      | term       |
      | top        |
      | dress      |
      | Men Tshirt |
acceptanceCriteria.text: The shop and the API agree on search results: when a shopper searches for "<term>" on the Products page, the products shown are exactly the products POST /api/searchProduct returns for "<term>", for the terms top, dress and Men Tshirt.
outcomes: for "top", the products shown are exactly those POST /api/searchProduct returns for "top"
for "dress", the products shown are exactly those POST /api/searchProduct returns for "dress"
for "Men Tshirt", the products shown are exactly those POST /api/searchProduct returns for "Men Tshirt"

acceptanceCriteria.quote:
Scenario: AC-11 No results on the Products page
    When a shopper searches for "zzqxv" on the Products page
    Then the grid is headed "Searched Products" and no product is shown
acceptanceCriteria.text: No results on the Products page: when a shopper searches for "zzqxv" on the Products page, the grid is headed "Searched Products" and no product is shown.
outcomes: the grid is headed "Searched Products"
no product is shown

endpoints.success: lists the products of the catalogue in a "products" array (story.md#L37)
endpoints.request: same host as the shop; form-encoded requests (story.md#L24); no parameters stated
same host as the shop; form-encoded body (story.md#L24) with the parameter search_product holding the search term (story.md#L26)

auth.mechanism: none: the product API is described as public

rules.text: Search matches the product name or its category name (the category under Women / Men / Kids, e.g. "Dress", "Tops", "Tops & Shirts", "Tshirts"); nothing else should come back. This replaces scenario AC-4 as written.
The brand is not a search field: searching "Polo" only finds products with "Polo" in the name or category.
Matching is a "contains" match, case-insensitive, as in AC-3.
Search terms are plain words or phrases, for example jean, top, dress, Men Tshirt; punctuation and special characters in search terms are out of scope.

errorModel.body: Bad request, search_product parameter is missing in POST request.

testData.strategy: none needed: read-only; every criterion searches or lists the existing catalogue, and nothing is created
constraints: AC-2 and AC-8 rely on the catalogue containing "Soft Stretch Jeans", "Regular Fit Straight Jeans" and "Grunt Blue Slim Fit Jeans" (story.md#L44)
AC-4 relies on the catalogue containing "Sleeves Top and Short - Blue & Pink" in Kids > Dress (story.md#L102)

gaps.element: what searching "dress" must return: AC-4 as written says only products with the term in their name; the Product Owner clarification says name or category name

tried.result: L52-L53: every product returned has the term in its product name, and every product whose name contains "dress" is returned; L100: PO comment "this replaces scenario AC-4 as written"; L102: name or category name, plus every product in a "Dress" category, nothing else; L103: brand is not a search field; L104: contains match, case-insensitive

gaps.value: searching "dress" returns every product whose name contains "dress" plus every product in a "Dress" category (e.g. "Sleeves Top and Short - Blue & Pink", Kids > Dress), and nothing else; brand is not searched
gaps.evidence: story.md#L100-L104 (PO clarification explicitly replaces AC-4 as written at L50-L53)

gaps.element: what "response code 400" refers to: the HTTP status of the response, or a response-code value carried in the response body

tried.result: L65 says "rejected with response code 400" without saying whether this is the HTTP status line or a field in the body; no other line describes the response format of errors

gaps.value: the HTTP status of the response is 400 (the usual meaning of "response code"). Alternative reading, not assumed: HTTP status is not constrained and a response-code value of 400 is carried in the body. Confirm with the Product Owner

gaps.element: field name that holds the category name inside a product's "category" (only "usertype" is named)

tried.result: L39 says the category holds the audience ("usertype") and the category name, but names no field for the category name
GET /api/productsList: each product has category = { usertype: { usertype: "Women" }, category: "Tops" }

gaps.value: category name is product.category.category; audience is product.category.usertype.usertype

gaps.element: shape of the POST /api/searchProduct response: where the list of matching products is carried and how a product is identified when comparing result sets

tried.result: L26 says the endpoint returns the products matching the term; the "products" array is only stated for GET /api/productsList (L37)
POST /api/searchProduct (form search_product=jean) answers a JSON body { responseCode, products: [ {id,name,price,brand,category} ] } served as Content-Type text/html

gaps.value: the matching products are in the body "products" array (same product shape as GET /api/productsList); a product is identified by "id"

gaps.element: what makes the no-match response "not an error": no status code or body is stated for a successful search

tried.result: L57 says "an empty product list is returned, not an error"; no success status is stated anywhere in the story

gaps.value: the response is a successful one carrying an empty product list: no error status and no error message (as in the AC-7 error case) is returned. No specific status code is asserted

gaps.element: where the error message of AC-7 is carried in the response (body field name / format)

tried.result: L66 gives the message text but not the field or format carrying it
POST /api/searchProduct without a body answers a JSON body { responseCode, message }

gaps.value: the message is carried in the body field "message"

gaps.element: UI locators on the Products page: search box, search button label, product grid heading and product cards (only the search box placeholder/label "Search Product" and the headings are stated)

/products: textbox "Search Product"; search button #submit_search (no accessible name, Enter does not submit); grid heading .features_items h2.title; product cards .features_items .productinfo p; search navigates to /products?search=<term>
